questions.question_text: Find the exact value of $\tan\left(\arcsin\left(-\frac{3}{7}\right)\right)$, with a rational denominator.

options.why: Took both legs of the triangle as positive and ignored that quadrant 4 makes the tangent negative.

questions.solution_text:
Let $\alpha=\arcsin\left(-\frac{3}{7}\right)$, so $\sin\alpha=-\frac{3}{7}$.
$-\frac{\pi}{2}\le\alpha\le\frac{\pi}{2}$ and $\sin\alpha<0$, so $\alpha$ is in quadrant 4.
$\text{adjacent}=\sqrt{7^{2}-3^{2}}$
$=\sqrt{40}$
$=2\sqrt{10}$
The tangent is negative in quadrant 4.
$\tan\alpha$

questions.question_text: Which expression equals $\cos\left(\arctan x\right)$ for all real $x$?

options.why: Used the sine ratio instead of the cosine ratio, giving $\sin\left(\arctan x\right)$.
Used subtraction from the $\arcsin x$ identity instead of the addition required by $1+\tan^{2}\alpha=1/\cos^{2}\alpha$.
Used the $\arcsin x$ identity and then took the tangent ratio, giving $\tan\left(\arcsin x\right)$.

questions.solution_text:
Let $\alpha=\arctan x$, so $\tan\alpha=x$.
$-\frac{\pi}{2}<\alpha<\frac{\pi}{2}$, so $\cos\alpha>0$.
Using $1+\tan^{2}\alpha=1/\cos^{2}\alpha$,
$\cos^{2}\alpha=\frac{1}{1+x^{2}}$.
Take the positive square root:
$\cos\left(\arctan x\right)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+x^{2}}}$.
At $x=0$, both sides are $1$.

questions.question_text: Find the exact value of $\tan\left(\arccos\left(-\frac{5}{9}\right)\right)$, with a rational denominator.

options.why: Found the reference-triangle tangent magnitude but ignored that the tangent is negative in quadrant 2.
Inverted the tangent ratio, using adjacent over opposite instead of opposite over adjacent.
Used opposite over hypotenuse, which gives $\sin\alpha$ instead of $\tan\alpha$.

questions.solution_text:
Let $\alpha=\arccos\left(-\frac{5}{9}\right)$, so $\cos\alpha=-\frac{5}{9}$.
$0\le\alpha\le\pi$ and $\cos\alpha<0$, so $\alpha$ is in quadrant 2.
The reference triangle has adjacent side $5$ and hypotenuse $9$.
$\text{opposite}=\sqrt{9^{2}-5^{2}}=\sqrt{56}=2\sqrt{14}$.
The tangent is negative in quadrant 2.
$\tan\alpha=-\frac{2\sqrt{14}}{5}$.
